settings.title: Settings
settings.drawThings.enabledDesc: Adds a draw_image tool to chats that calls Draw Things on this computer or your local network.
settings.drawThings.apiUrlDesc: The HTTP API Server address exposed by Draw Things.
settings.drawThings.networkHint: Use http://127.0.0.1:7860 on the same Mac. From Windows, enter the Mac's LAN address, for example http://192.168.1.20:7860.
settings.drawThings.testFailed: The Draw Things connection test failed.
settings.drawThings.autoLaunchDesc: If the local API is not running, open Draw Things on this Mac and retry automatically.
settings.drawThings.setupStep1: In Draw Things, open Settings → Advanced → API Server.
settings.drawThings.setupStep2: Enable API Server, choose HTTP, and keep the default port 7860.
settings.drawThings.setupStep3: Return here and test the connection. You can then ask for an image directly in chat.
settings.drawThings.resultHint: Generated images are saved under generated-images in the current chat project and uploaded back to the Open WebUI conversation automatically.
settings.asuswrtMcp.enabledDesc: Let Open WebUI observe your router and run a small set of confirmation-gated actions over SSH.
settings.asuswrtMcp.connectionDesc: Use a LAN or ZeroTier/Tailscale-reachable address. Do not expose router SSH to the public internet.
settings.asuswrtMcp.hostHint: Example: 192.168.50.1 or a private overlay address
settings.asuswrtMcp.keyHint: The key stays on this computer; only its path is stored.
settings.asuswrtMcp.knownHostsHint: Pin the router host key here. Leave empty only for a first LAN demo.
settings.asuswrtMcp.saveFailed: Could not save ASUSWRT MCP settings.
settings.asuswrtMcp.securityStep1: Enable SSH on the router as LAN only and prefer an authorized key.
settings.asuswrtMcp.securityStep2: The MCP server exposes allow-listed read-only queries; control actions require explicit confirmation.
settings.asuswrtMcp.securityStep3: Remote access should use ZeroTier or Tailscale, not WAN port forwarding.
